review_notes: Read the whole target file plus the relevant parts of SphereTranslation.lean (translate, ambient, translate_zero, ambient_zero) and Embedding.lean (standardEmbedding lemmas). translateCoordinate is not used outside this file. I found no simp cycle and no competing rules. The one concern is a missing simp interface for the new definition. It is a modest finding. I did not check Lean behavior, and I did not check whether a coe_translate lemma already exists elsewhere (my grep over SphereTranslation.lean did not show one).

findings.excerpt: fun y => ((f y).1, fun j => if j = i then
findings.problem: translateCoordinate is a new def with no companion simp lemmas. There is no `(translateCoordinate i C f y).1 = (f y).1` lemma. There are no `.2 i` or `.2 j` lemmas for j = i and j ≠ i. There is no lemma that `standardEmbedding q (translateCoordinate i C f y)` is the ambient coordinate update. There is no `translateCoordinate i 0 f = f` lemma, even though `translate_zero` is already simp. The only way to compute with it is to unfold it. The proof does this with `simp only [standardEmbedding, translateCoordinate, G, ..., SphereTranslation.translate]`. That unfolds both the new def and `SphereTranslation.translate` to raw subtype constructors, in both branches. Any later user of the definition has to repeat this unfolding and leaks the `if j = i` representation.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas after the definition. These are `translateCoordinate_fst` and `translateCoordinate_snd_self` (for j = i, giving `translate (C y) ((f y).2 i)`). A third is `translateCoordinate_snd_of_ne` (for j ≠ i, giving `(f y).2 j`). A fourth is a `standardEmbedding` form stating that the j-th coordinate of the embedding is `ambient (C y) (…)` at i and unchanged elsewhere. Optionally add `translateCoordinate_zero` with C = fun _ => 0, which follows from `translate_zero`. Add a simp lemma for the coercion `(translate c x).1 = ambient c x.1`, with `rfl` as proof. Then the two simp-only calls at lines 83–87 can use these named lemmas instead of unfolding the definitions.
findings.benefit: Users get a canonical normal form that works under simp. The proof stops depending on the internal `if`/subtype representation. Later results about translateCoordinate, such as composition or the zero case, can be proved by simp rather than by unfolding.
